title: Rome 1527: The City Sacked by an Army That Was Never Paid
summary: Tells how, on the sixth of May, fifteen twenty-seven, the army of Emperor Charles the Fifth, unpaid for months and in open mutiny, burst into Rome after its commander, the Duke of Bourbon, was shot on the walls, and sacked the city for months. The episode ranges from the stroke Frundsberg suffered while trying to calm his army, to the Swiss Guard wiped out before Saint Peter's, to the captivity of Pope Clement the Seventh, who fled along the Passetto to Castel Sant'Angelo, and then covers how that captivity paved the way for England's break with Rome over Henry the Eighth's divorce.
